name: Juice Dollar
oneLiner: JUSD is Juice Dollar's Citrea dollar, minted through oracle-free BTC positions or 1:1 stablecoin bridge reserves using a Frankencoin/d-EURO architecture.
collateral: Wrapped cBTC (WCBTC, the Citrea Bitcoin L2 native-coin wrapper) deposited in oracle-free overcollateralized positions, plus StablecoinBridge routes that mint JUSD 1:1 against external Citrea stablecoins USDC.e, USDT.e and ctUSD (Citrea USD); protocol is a d-EURO / Frankencoin (ZCHF) architecture fork.
pegMechanism: Overcollateralized minting against BTC collateral on Citrea with automated on-chain liquidations when collateral ratios fall below required thresholds; no external price oracles; positions and debt are verifiable on-chain (Frankencoin-style design)

oracleRisk.summary: JuiceDollar's tracked WCBTC CDP path uses permissionless challenges and Dutch auctions to discover collateral price and liquidate positions, explicitly replacing an external oracle.

branchApplicability.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 data research
branchApplicability.rationale: JuiceDollar documents the WCBTC position path as an oracle-free challenge system: a challenger starts an auction, the Dutch auction discovers the collateral market price, and a bid below the position liquidation price completes liquidation. The tracked stablecoin bridge routes are separate 1:1 conversions and do not create borrower collateral branches, so there is no external feed branch to inventory.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: CitreaScan marks the deployed JUSD contract verified, and its verified source and ABI expose standard transfer and transferFrom operations with no holder blacklist, freeze, pause, seizure, or global transfer-stop function. At Citrea block 9985719, owner() reverted, reserve() resolved to Equity 0x2a36f2b204b46fd82653cd06d00c7ff757c99ae4, and EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots were zero. StablecoinBridge emergencyStop halts bridge issuance but allows users to burn JUSD for its stablecoin; it does not stop native JUSD transfers. Issuer docs and legal materials, GitHub, the explorer, pinned RPC, and the legacy-explorer archive were reviewed; no standalone reserve attestation or transparency report is used for this code-level access conclusion.

blacklistabilityReview.upstreamSuppressionRationale: USDC.e, USDT.e, and ctUSD issuer controls can impair bridge collateral or redemption, but Citrea's verified JUSD source does not expose them as native JUSD holder-balance controls; those remain reserve and bridge risks.

reserveReview.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-3 (lead usdd-tron-dao-reserve)
reserveReview.rationale: Composition re-derived from issuer-side data on 2026-07-20, replacing the previous 99.999% BTC / 0.001% bridge placeholder. The JuiceDollar API collateral stats report zero WCBTC held across all positions (80 total, 2 open), and both open positions are dust clones with collateralBalance 0 and 56 JUSD principal each. JUSD totalSupply is 56,695.50 (API stablecoin info). Citrea RPC reads at the latest block show StablecoinBridgeUSDT (0x5CC0e668...0614) holding 56,695.422933 USDT.e (token 0x9f3096bac87e7f03dc09b0b416eb0df837304dc4, 6 decimals) against 56,695.4225 JUSD minted through it - about 99.9999% of supply. The USDC.e and ctUSD bridges hold only $0.069 and $0.010 respectively, and the StartUSD bridge is empty. JUSD is therefore currently backed ~100% by bridged USDT.e in the USDT bridge, not by BTC collateral; the BTC CDP path remains live and the composition will shift back if positions are funded. USDT.e is mapped to usdt-tether as a collateral dependency, matching the repo's bridged-stablecoin convention; the slice keeps the low stablecoin tier with custody/smart-contract risk factors covering the Citrea canonical-bridge layer.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: JuiceDollar public API and Citrea mainnet RPC reads on 2026-07-20 (bridge stablecoin balances, bridge minted counters, open-position collateral)
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Residuals below rounding: dust USDC.e ($0.07) and ctUSD ($0.01) bridge balances, 112 JUSD of uncollateralized dust-position principal, and the small JUICE equity pool (~$1.7k). The WCBTC position path is live but holds zero collateral today, so no BTC slice is carried at this composition date.

providers.name: JuiceDollar StablecoinBridge and position contracts (ownerless, non-upgradeable) on Citrea - self-custodied, no third-party custodian

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-3 (lead usdd-tron-dao-reserve)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: At the JUSD layer there is no legal custodian: the reviewed StablecoinBridge source (pinned commit) holds the bridged stable and releases it only against JUSD burns, with an emergencyStop that halts issuance but still lets users burn JUSD for the underlying; position contracts likewise hold WCBTC until repayment or liquidation, so no redeployment or rehypothecation path exists in contract logic. There is no trust, SPV, or holder-claim structure, hence bankruptcyRemoteness none. What is not established here: the custody of native USDT backing USDT.e inside Citrea's canonical bridge (an upstream dependency outside the JuiceDollar contracts), the Citrea bridge's operator/security model, and any off-chain arrangements of the team or gateways. USDT.e issuer freeze risk (Tether) applies to the bridge-held balance, as flagged by the blacklistable marker.

mintAuthority.summary: JUSD is an ownerless Frankencoin fork on Citrea. owner() reverts and there is no EIP-1967 proxy admin. mint() is gated to registered minters, but an accepted minter can mint an unrestricted amount; qualified JUICE pool-share holders can veto proposed minters during the application period.

controls.label: JUSD accepted-minter authorization registry
controls.capDescription: There is no numeric per-minter mint cap. After its application period, an accepted minter can call mint() for an unrestricted amount; a candidate is subject to a qualified Equity-holder veto before acceptance.
controls.evidence: The Citrea manifest and CitreaScan verified source identify this deployed JUSD token. Its minters mapping gates mint(), while suggestMinter adds a candidate only for the application period during which Equity can veto it. Once accepted, the deployed mint() function has no numeric amount cap. At Citrea block 9984927, owner() reverted and both EIP-1967 slots were zero.

controls.label: JUICE pool-share holder veto governance
controls.capDescription: Qualified JUICE pool-share holders can veto proposed minters during the application period, but the Equity contract cannot mint, set a mint cap, or change mint parameters.
controls.evidence: The Citrea manifest identifies this Equity contract, and JUSD reserve() returned it at block 9984927. Equity's qualified pool-share voting and checkQualified guard supply the veto path for proposed JUSD minters; it does not mint, set a mint cap, or change mint parameters.

review.evidence: The pinned JuiceDollar source and CitreaScan verified deployed source make minting contingent on the token's registered minters mapping, but an accepted minter's mint() call has no numeric amount cap. Equity-qualified pool-share holders can veto candidates only during minter application. At Citrea block 9984927, the token's owner() call reverted, reserve() returned Equity 0x2a36f2b204b46fd82653cd06d00c7ff757c99ae4, and EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots were zero. The two reviewed control addresses therefore identify the authorization registry and its governance veto, with no proxy upgrade path.
